content.title: RAPID REACTION: Last second tip-in sends Purdue past Texas in Sweet 16
content.text: March 25, 2026Updated March 26, 2026, 9:19 p.m. CTDespite a heroic effort, the Texas Longhorns men's basketball season is over after losing to Purdue in the Sweet 16, 79-77. All-American point guard Braden Smith drove to the basket with seconds remaining, but missed. Trey Kaufman-Renn forced his way past Dailyn Swain to get the rebound tip-in with less than a second left for the game winner.On the bench with four fouls, Texas center Matas Vokietaitis was not in the game to provide a stronger interior defense on the final Purdue possession. The big Lithuanian didn't not have the numbers he's had over the course of the NCAA Tournament. But's also understandable because the Boilermakers have the best inside game Texas has faced.The game was back and forth from the opening tip-off. There were ten ties and 16 lead changes. The game was very back and forth over the last few minutes of the second half.Texas was paced by a legendary performance by senior guard Tramon Mark. Mark led all scorers in the game with 29 points. A big total, especially considering it looked like he severely twisted his ankle and needed the UT trainers to re-tape his ankle several times.Dailyn Swain, who started slow, ended up with 15-points. Jordan Pope, also playing on a hurt angle, added 12 points and Vokietaitis had nine.- Final -Second Half: Texas 77, Purdue 79Kaufman-Renn wins it for PurdueTrey Kaufman-Renn fought for position on Dailyn Swain under the basket and got an offensive rebound tip-in with less than a second left to send Purdue to the Elite Eight. Texas season ends valiantly, but it wasn't enough.Swain three-point playDailyn Swain drove to the basket, turned the corner and hit a layup and was fouled by Oscar Cluff. Cluff has foulded out.Cox hits his FTsTexas fouled C.J. Cox to put him on the line. He made both of his shots.Vokietaitis makes his FTsPurdue fouled Matas Vokietaitis to put him on the line. He made both FTs. :19.4 leftPope Misses ThreeTexas coach Sean Miller ran a play to get Pope open. It worked but Pope missed the shot. Texas then tied up the ball to keep possession with :21 to go.All-American MomentPurdue's Braden Smith drove right to the basket like a veteran to give the Boilermakers a three-point lead with :38 left.Weaver Follow puts UT within oneA Dailyn Swain miss was put back by an alert Chendall Weaver to cut the Boilermakers lead to one point with :59 left.Cluff gives Purdue leadOscar Cluff's layup with three minutes left has given the Boilermakers the lead.Heide Fouls outCam Heide might have been too hyped up against his old team. The Texas forward has fouled out with five minutes left.Mark stays red hotTramon Mark, who leads all scorers in the game, hit a big three-pointer to give UT the lead.Vokietaitis back, draws foulPlaying with four fouls of his own, Matas Vokietaitis draws the fourth foul on Oscar Cluff.Purdue in the BonusTexas has committed its sixth foul of the half. Purdue is now in the bonus for the rest of the game.Purdue Takes leadA rebound and kick-out to Fletcher Loyer for a three-pointer has given the Boilermakers a lead.Extra PointAfter a review during a time out, an earlier bucket by Joran Pope was upgraded from a two-pointer to a three-pointer. That gives Texas a one-point lead with 10:20 left in the game,Mark again!A run by the Boilermakers had given Purdue the lead. But continuing his hot play, Tramon Mark nailed a three-ball to tie the game.Bad Vokietaitis FoulLithuanian Matas Vokietaitis has committed his third foul and is on the bench. There was no need for him to foul in that spot.Purdue Ties itTwo turnovers by Dailyn Swain have led to four points for the Boilermakers.Mark re-tapping ankleThe UT trainers are working on Tramon Mark's ankle. They are re-tapping it hoping he can keep playing.Heide haunts his old teamCam Heide, who transferred to Texas from Purdue, hits a big three-pointer against his old team. Of course, Heide had what amounted to the clinching shot against Gonzaga.Mark twists ankleAs Tramon Mark fired a three-pointer from the top of the circle he was fouled by Fletcher Loyer. Mark looked to twist his ankle. After laying on the court for a bit and walking it off, he made two of three free throws.Swain much more aggressiveDailyn Swain has come out of the locker room on a mission. He's driving to the bucket much more and has three points and an assist so far.Mark starts where he left offTramon Mark's three-pointer kicks off the scoring in the second half.- Halftime -First Half: Texas 35, Purdue 39Pope buries a threeHis ankle hurt but Joran Pope has shown up to play. His three-pointer from the corner has cut the Purdue lead to two points and caused coach Matt Painter to call time out.Swain halts Boilermakers runPurdue went on a 7-0 that was snapped by a Dailyn Swain layup.Vokietaitis ElbowAn elbow that was originally called foul by Matas Vokietaitis on C.J. Cox was reviewed to see if it was a flagrant foul. It was ruled it a dead ball contact foul. Purdue got two free throws and the ball with three minutes left in the first half,Swain ScoresTexas' leading scoring Dailyn Swain has been quiet so far, but his bucket ties the game at 30-30. That followed a big three from Jordan Pope.Miller preaches defense"Offense isn't our problem. We have a major problem on defense right now. Obviously, Purdue is the best at what they do. But we have to be able to give them more resistance to have an opportunity to win." - Texas coach Sean Miller during first half time outWeaver Throws it DownChendall Weaver's put-back dunk breaks a streak of missed shots by Texas.Mark on the MarkTramon Mark is the hottest player in the game so far. The senior guard leads all scorers with 12-points midway through the first half.Texas takes first leadFive quick points by Tramon Mark has given Texas its first lead. Nic Codie added a three-ball of his own.Pope Three ties scoreA big question coming into the game was the status of Jordan Pope. He is starting and his three-pointer has tied the score.Lithuanian HammerTexas center Matas Vokietaitis grabbed an offensive rebound and threw down a dunk to cut it to one.All threes to openPurdue started teh game with two quick three-pointers. Texas's Tramon Mark answered with one of his own.Pope to StartSark is in the HousePope Joins WarmupsLonghorns Boulevard WestPope a game-time decisionThe Longhorns are in the buildingPractice PicsQuick WorkoutAir Corgi Likes the HornsIt's a workdayLatest Injury UpdateArizona ConnectionLithuanian PrideMic Check, testingHeide reflects on time with PurdueCamden Heide spent three seasons in West Lafayette, Indiana. He redshirted then played two seasons for coach Matt Painter. He was asked about his memories as a Boilermaker.Center of AttentionPlayers speak with reporters during a locker room press availability.Texas has arrived in San JoseMiller Talks Texas with Jim RomePainter on MillerFull Purdue Boilermakers PreviewThe Longhorns are onto the Sweet Sixteen and has the Purdue Boilermakers awaiting them. Braden Smith, NCAA record holder, leads an elite offense with four players averaging double figures scoring. FULL STORYFive reasons Texas can upset PurdueTexas has roared into the NCAA Tournament's Sweet Sixteen with a string up upsets and solid performances. Purdue features the biggest test yet.See: Five reasons Texas Longhorns basketball can upset Purdue BoilermakersTexas getting key contributionsWhen Texas takes on Purdue, it'll be a challenge for the defense. Weaver and Codie could make the challenge much more manageable.See: Chendall Weaver, Nic Codie can send Texas to the Elite EightSee: Texas getting key contribution off bench from Nic CodieTexas Longhorns Road to Sweet 16Showing Coach Miller some loveTexas vs. Purdue Tournament HistoryWhen does Texas basketball play in the Sweet 16? The Longhorns play the Purdue Boilermakers on Thursday in San Jose at SAP Center at 6:10 p.m. CT.Texas vs. Purdue game infoGame day: March 26, 2026Game time: 6:10 p.m. CTLocation: San Jose, CaliforniaArena: SAP CenterWhat channel is Texas vs. Purdue game on?The game is on CBS and can be streamed on Fubo.Texas vs. Purdue TV infoTelevision: CBSAnnouncers: Play-by-Play: Brian AndersonAnalyst: Jim JacksonReporter: Allie LaForceLive stream: Watch on Fubo (Regional restrictions may apply)Watch Texas vs. Purdue on FuboTexas vs. Purdue line, odds, spread, over/underSpread favorite: Purdue (-7.5)Moneyline: Texas +260 / Gonzaga -325Total (Over/Under): 148.5 (Odds provided by BetMGM)Purdue Boiler Makers Injury ReportC.J. Cox - GuardPurdue sophomore C.J. Cox suffered an apparent knee injury early in the second half of Purdue's win over Miami in the second round. He did not return to the game. Coach Matt Painter told reporters after the game that Cox had "hyperextended" his knee and would see how it responded to treatment this week.Cox called it "nothing serious" and said he could have re-entered the game if needed. He has started every game for the Boilermakers this season, while averaging 8.5 points, 2.6 rebounds and 1.3 assists.Texas Longhorns Injury ReportJordan Pope - GuardTexas senior guard Jordan Pope was limping pretty significantly late in Texas' win over Gonzaga in the second round. The senior guard walked to the locker room under his own power, but several staff members were by his side."He's dealing with a lower leg situation," Texas coach Sean Miller said Wednesday. "We're hopeful that he can (play). We've given him a lot of rest since our last game, and I think he's really responding to it. We still had a pretty quick turnaround, all things considered, because of the distance between San Jose and Austin and traveling from Dayton to Portland and Portland back to Austin.”Pope says he's 100% going to play against the Boilermakers. "I'll be fine," Pope said after the game.Texas Longhorns 2026 NCAA Tournament ResultsFirst Four: Texas 68, NC State 66 (Game Coverage)First Round: (11) Texas 79, (6) BYU 71 (Game Coverage)Second Round: (11) Texas 74, (3) Gonzaga 68 (Game Coverage)Purdue Boilermakers 2026 NCAA Tournament ResultsFirst Round: (2) Purdue 104, (15) Queens 71Second Round: (2) Purdue 79, (7) Miami 69Texas Longhorns NCAA Tournament Photos Texas vs. Purdue Prediction Can the Texas Longhorns keep the magic flowing? The Longhorns might be playing the best they have all season thanks to a couple tweaks by first year coach Sean Miller. Miller made Matas Vokeitaitis the focus of the offense.But Purdue is a proper opponent from the Big Ten, arguably the best conference in college basketball in 2026. Purdue has the best point guard in the nation in Braden Smith. A late-season surge from Trey Kaufman-Renn and Fletcher Loyer has taken Purdue to a real national title contender.Prediction: Purdue 74, Texas 66
